area_note: Very small core. The entire register file is only 1024 bits (32 words). A 16-word internal coprocessor buffer (512 bits) is massive on this scale and should be avoided.
constraints: The coprocessor interface cannot access memory.
Operands from memory must be loaded into CPU registers first (using standard LW), then passed to the custom instruction.
A custom instruction can only accept up to two 32-bit operands at a time (rs1, rs2).
A custom instruction can only return one 32-bit result (rd) per invocation.
Do not build stateful buffers in the coprocessor that rival the CPU's register file in size.
coprocessor: Pico Co-Processor Interface (PCPI). Receives full 32-bit instruction word, plus rs1 and rs2 register values.
coprocessor_result: 32 bits via pcpi_rd, written to the CPU register file when pcpi_wr and pcpi_ready are asserted.
custom_opcode_space: Any opcode not natively decoded by the base core traps to the PCPI interface, making all standard RISC-V custom-0 through custom-3 spaces available.
evidence: picorv32.v ports: pcpi_valid, pcpi_insn, pcpi_rs1, pcpi_rs2, pcpi_wr, pcpi_rd, pcpi_ready, pcpi_wait. No memory signals exist on this interface.
picorv32.v main state machine (cpu_state_fetch, cpu_state_ld_rs1, cpu_state_exec) proves multi-cycle execution.
picorv32.v (instr_trap definition): Any unrecognized instruction asserts pcpi_valid and delegates execution to the coprocessor.
isa: RV32I with optional E, M, and C extensions (configured via ENABLE_REGS_16_31, ENABLE_MUL, ENABLE_DIV, COMPRESSED_ISA parameters).
memory_interface: Simple synchronous valid/ready handshake for 32-bit words (mem_valid, mem_ready, mem_wstrb).
microarchitecture: Multi-cycle, non-pipelined state machine (fetch -> decode/ld -> exec -> mem -> fetch).
name: PicoRV32
register_file: 32 (or 16) registers. 1 write port. 2 read ports if ENABLE_REGS_DUALPORT=1, otherwise 1 read port.
